# Previews: next steps

Generated by `patchy setup previews` (patchy v0.12.40) for the **Cloudflare Tunnel** recipe on **k3s**.
Previews will be served at `https://<project>-<issue>.acme-previews.dev`, and viewers sign in at `https://preview-auth.acme.dev`.
Nothing here has been applied: run the steps below in order. Running `patchy setup previews` again shows what would
change before it replaces a file, and never draws a new Dex client secret unless you pass
`--rotate dex-client-secret`.

`patchy setup previews -n patchy --apply --values <your values> --chart-version <version>` runs the in-cluster
steps below for you, in order, with your kubeconfig and helm, stopping at the first failure (add `--dry-run` to list
them first). Preview nodes, image pulls, Dex's static client, the DNS records stay yours.

## Files

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `NEXT-STEPS.md` | This file. |
| `answers.yaml` | Every answer, the edge and the CLI version: a re-run starts from it. No secret. |
| `manifests/cloudflared.yaml` | cloudflared's namespace, config, Deployment (2026.10.1, by digest) and NetworkPolicy. |
| `patchy-previews.values.yaml` | patchy's chart values for previews, layered after your own. |
| `secrets/cloudflared-credentials.secret.yaml` | The tunnel's credentials, in cloudflared's namespace (0600). |
| `secrets/dex-patchy-preview-auth-client.secret.yaml` | The same secret, in Dex's namespace, for its static client (0600). |
| `secrets/patchy-preview-auth-dex.secret.yaml` | The relay's Dex client secret, in the release namespace (0600). |

The files under `secrets/` (mode 0600) hold the only copy of the Dex client secret and of the tunnel credentials. Apply them, or encrypt them (sops,
sealed-secrets) before they go anywhere else; never commit them as they are.

## 1. Before you start

- patchy is installed in namespace `patchy` as release `patchy`, with `intentController.enabled: true`
  in your values: previews are built for intents, and the preview-controller needs intent-controller.
- NetworkPolicy is enforced. k3s enforces it with its embedded kube-router unless the server runs with `--disable-network-policy`.
- Both names sit on zones in your Cloudflare account: `acme-previews.dev` for the previews and `acme.dev` for the
  sign-in host. Two registrable domains keep preview code off sign-in's site; with only one domain, register a second,
  cheap one for previews, or accept sharing it with `--shared-domain acknowledged`. A preview suffix that is a whole
  zone is also what lets Cloudflare's free certificate cover the previews.
- The locally-managed tunnel `6ff42ae2-765d-4adf-8112-31c55c1551ef` exists. You created it on your workstation, where its login certificate
  stays (`cert.pem` never enters the cluster):

  ```sh
  cloudflared tunnel login
  cloudflared tunnel create patchy-previews
  ```

  and this command read its credentials file (`~/.cloudflared/6ff42ae2-765d-4adf-8112-31c55c1551ef.json`) into `secrets/cloudflared-credentials.secret.yaml`.
- Cloudflare's edge terminates TLS for both names, so Cloudflare sees preview traffic in the clear. Previews should
  hold staging data only.

## 2. Preview nodes

Every slot Pod selects `patchy.bitwisemedia.uk/previews=true` and tolerates the taint `patchy.bitwisemedia.uk/preview-only=true:NoExecute`. Add at least one node with both, set when it registers so no other Pod lands on it first.

```sh
curl -sfL https://get.k3s.io | K3S_URL=https://<server>:6443 K3S_TOKEN=<token> sh -s - agent \
  --node-label patchy.bitwisemedia.uk/previews=true --node-taint patchy.bitwisemedia.uk/preview-only=true:NoExecute
```

`patchy-previews.values.yaml` sets `preview.nodeIsolation` over your own values, but Helm merges its `selector` map: remove any `preview.nodeIsolation.selector` from your own values, or Pods require those labels too.

Never `kubectl taint` a node that already runs Pods: those Pods would be evicted, and new ones could land before the taint.

## 3. Preview image pulls

Preview images are `ghcr.io/acme/patchy/previews/<app>:sha-<commit>`. Slot Pods may not reference a Secret, so pulls are
the node's own: a private registry needs credentials on the preview nodes only: k3s's `registries.yaml` (`configs."ghcr.io".auth`) or a kubelet credential provider, with a key that can pull `acme/patchy/previews/*` and nothing else. Public images need nothing, but make preview images of private code public only knowingly.

## 4. Dex

Add the relay's static client to Dex's configuration, with its one redirect URI:

```yaml
staticClients:
  - id: patchy-preview-auth
    name: patchy previews
    secretEnv: PATCHY_PREVIEW_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET
    redirectURIs:
      - https://preview-auth.acme.dev/dex/callback
```

Give Dex the secret in that environment variable from the Secret in its namespace (with Dex's Helm chart:
`envVars: [{name: PATCHY_PREVIEW_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: patchy-preview-auth-client, key: clientSecret}}}]`),
then roll Dex:

```sh
kubectl apply -f secrets/dex-patchy-preview-auth-client.secret.yaml
```

## 5. TLS

Cloudflare's edge holds both certificates; nothing in the cluster does, and cloudflared reaches the gateway inside the
cluster over plain HTTP. Universal SSL, free on every plan, covers each zone's apex and first-level names: `*.acme-previews.dev` and
`preview-auth.acme.dev` are both, so there is nothing to order. Turn on **Always Use HTTPS** in both zones.

## 6. Install

cloudflared runs in namespace `patchy-cloudflared`, which its manifest creates (a new namespace of its own:
rolling back deletes it), with the tunnel credentials mounted from Secret `cloudflared-credentials` and egress to DNS,
the gateway and any public address on 443 and 7844 (TCP and QUIC), where Cloudflare's edge answers, alone:

```sh
kubectl apply -f manifests/cloudflared.yaml -f secrets/cloudflared-credentials.secret.yaml
kubectl -n patchy-cloudflared rollout status deployment/cloudflared
```

It sends `*.acme-previews.dev` and `preview-auth.acme.dev` to `patchy-preview-gateway` and answers 404 for any other name. cloudflared
reaches the gateway from its own Pod addresses, so the values set `previewAuth.ingressFrom: []` (the chart's default:
the relay's ports admit any source), overriding any narrowing to a load balancer's subnets in your values; to narrow it
again, list cloudflared's Pod CIDRs there too. Then patchy:

```sh
kubectl apply -f secrets/patchy-preview-auth-dex.secret.yaml
helm upgrade patchy oci://ghcr.io/devthenet-labs/patchy/charts/patchy -n patchy --version 0.12.40 \
  -f <your values> -f patchy-previews.values.yaml
```

One upgrade: the gateway needs no permit stage. `previewController.config.apiServerCIDR: auto` is looked up at render time, so it needs `helm upgrade` against the cluster (not
`helm template` or a GitOps render, which must set the kubernetes Service's `/32` instead).

## 7. DNS

Two proxied records, each a CNAME to `6ff42ae2-765d-4adf-8112-31c55c1551ef.cfargotunnel.com`:

- `*.acme-previews.dev`
- `preview-auth.acme.dev`

```sh
cloudflared tunnel route dns 6ff42ae2-765d-4adf-8112-31c55c1551ef '*.acme-previews.dev'
```

`cloudflared tunnel route dns` writes into the zone of the `cert.pem` that `cloudflared tunnel login` chose, so it
creates the wildcard when you chose `acme-previews.dev`. Create the sign-in host's record in `acme.dev`'s DNS
settings by hand (a proxied CNAME `preview-auth.acme.dev` to `6ff42ae2-765d-4adf-8112-31c55c1551ef.cfargotunnel.com`), or run `cloudflared tunnel login`
again for that zone and `cloudflared tunnel --origincert <its cert.pem> route dns 6ff42ae2-765d-4adf-8112-31c55c1551ef preview-auth.acme.dev`.

Then, in `acme-previews.dev`, add a Cache Rule that bypasses the cache for every request whose host ends in
`.acme-previews.dev`: Cloudflare honours the gateway's `private`, but a rule that caches by file extension does not, and
would serve one viewer's preview to another. Keep the allowlist at Cloudflare too, if you want one (a WAF custom rule,
or Cloudflare Access): `previewAuth.gateway.forwardedHops` is 1 (Cloudflare's edge appends the viewer's address to
`X-Forwarded-For`; cloudflared adds none), and `inboundCIDRs` stays empty. A proxied record resolves to Cloudflare's
addresses, not the cluster's, so `patchy check previews` skips its DNS line: check both records in the dashboard.

## 8. Check

```sh
patchy check previews -n patchy
```

Every line should PASS before the first intent's preview is opened.

## Rolling back

In reverse order, all by deletion:

1. Set `previewAuth.gateway.enabled: false` (or `preview.enabled: false`) and run the same `helm upgrade`.
2. `kubectl delete -f manifests/cloudflared.yaml`, which deletes namespace `patchy-cloudflared` and the tunnel
   credentials' Secret with it.
3. Remove the two DNS records. Then delete the tunnel on your workstation (`cloudflared tunnel delete
   6ff42ae2-765d-4adf-8112-31c55c1551ef`): its credentials stop working everywhere they were copied.
4. Remove the static client from Dex, and delete the Secrets (`kubectl delete --ignore-not-found -f secrets/`).
5. Delete what the chart keeps on uninstall, as `docs/intents/preview-sign-in.md` lists it.
